result.topic_en: Euler derives the minimum slope (declivity) of a tube or river bed needed for water to flow against friction, expressing it per thousand feet of distance as a function of river depth g.
result.transcription:
372 TENTAMEN THEORIAE

90. Si altitudo vasis $AB=a$ sit quam minima, patet effluxum non dari, nisi sit $g\cos.\zeta < \alpha l$, seu, nisi sinus decliuitatis tubi maior sit, quam $\frac{\alpha l}{g}$. Quodsi ergo ponatur $g=n\alpha l=0,0075\,n$ pedum, vt aqua per tubum BC defluat, necesse est, vt sit $\cos.\zeta > \frac{g}{n}$. Si ergo sit vel $n=1$, vel $n<1$, aqua per istiusmodi tubum plane non defluet; quare, vt aqua defluat, necesse est, vt sit $n>1$, seu $g>\alpha l$, ac tum sinus decliuitatis maior esse debet, quam $\frac{1}{n}$.

91. Hinc pro fluminibus decliuitas aluei assignari potest, vt aqua decurrat, ita vt si decliuitas minor esset, aqua esset stagnatura. Pendet autem haec decliuitas a littera $g$, qua profunditas fluuii indicatur. Vt igitur hanc decliuitatem pro quauis fluminis profunditate definiamus, sit pro distantia mille pedum altitudo, per quam alueus subsidit, $=z$ ped. eritque $\frac{z}{1000}$ sinus decliuitatis. Quare si fluuii profunditas sit $g$ pedum, ob $g=\frac{3}{400}n$, et $n=\frac{400}{3}g$, fiet $\frac{z}{1000}>\frac{3}{400g}$: vt ergo aqua in alueo defluat, oportet sit $z>\frac{30}{4g}$, seu $z>\frac{1000\alpha l}{g}$.

92. Pro quauis ergo fluminis profunditate $g$ definire poterimus decliuitatem aluei, quae distantiae mille pedum conueniat, vbi aqua primum fluxum consequatur: ita vt, si decliuitas esset minor, aqua esset stagnatura, vti sequens tabella habet.

items.english: If therefore n = 1 or n < 1, water will not flow at all through such a tube; hence for the water to flow it is necessary that n > 1, i.e. g > αl, and then the sine of the declivity must be greater than 1/n.
